prompt: Which critical value $z^*$ is used for a $90\%$ confidence interval?
hint: A $90\%$ interval leaves $10\%$ outside, split as $5\%$ in each tail.

hints.text: A $90\%$ interval leaves $10\%$ outside, split as $5\%$ in each tail.
$z^*$ is the value with $5\%$ of the standard normal curve above it. Recall: $1.96$ cuts off $2.5\%$, $2.576$ cuts off $0.5\%$.

explanation: For confidence level $C$, $z^*$ is the value such that the middle $C$ of the standard normal curve lies between $-z^*$ and $z^*$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Order them by confidence
steps: More confidence needs a wider interval, so a bigger $z^*$.
